executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 indicates multiple concurrent disease threats across Europe and the Americas. The most significant signals include ongoing avian influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, a resurgent pertussis cycle, and dengue transmission at elevated levels. The start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season in April 2026 coincides with continued RSV co-circulation, increasing respiratory disease burden across multiple regions.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous threats—including H5N1 spillover risk, dengue surge, pertussis resurgence, and a new Southern Hemisphere influenza season—demand coordinated surveillance and rapid response across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating ongoing animal-to-human spillover risk
Sustained H5N1 circulation in poultry and wild birds across the Americas with documented human exposure events
threats.action: Enhance zoonotic surveillance at human-animal interface, enforce biosafety protocols for exposed workers, and pre-position antiviral stockpiles

threats.name: Dengue Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 suggesting elevated transmission
Historically high dengue burden in the Americas with year-round endemic circulation in multiple countries
threats.action: Strengthen vector control programs, enhance case detection and serotyping, and issue public health advisories in affected countries

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained or worsening transmission
Multi-month alert cadence suggests a cyclical resurgence consistent with waning immunity patterns
threats.action: Review vaccination coverage gaps particularly in infants and pregnant women, investigate potential waning immunity in older cohorts, and reinforce booster campaigns

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza
signals: PAHO alert issued 27 April 2026 marking the start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Prior alert in January 2026 noted simultaneous influenza and RSV co-circulation, compounding healthcare system pressure
threats.action: Accelerate Southern Hemisphere vaccination campaigns, monitor strain match with current vaccine formulation, and prepare healthcare surge capacity

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued 23 April 2026 indicating continued transmission in the Americas
Ongoing global mpox activity with clade-specific concerns elevates regional risk
threats.action: Maintain ring vaccination strategies, strengthen contact tracing networks, and ensure diagnostic capacity at regional reference laboratories

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating measles activity in the region
Risk amplified by pandemic-era immunization gaps and population movement
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments, implement supplementary immunization activities in under-vaccinated populations, and enforce outbreak response protocols

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 signaling active yellow fever risk
Epizootics in non-human primates often precede human spillover events in endemic zones
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers, monitor non-human primate die-offs as early warning signals, and enforce entry vaccination requirements

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating chikungunya activity
Co-circulation with dengue and Zika complicates clinical diagnosis and surveillance accuracy
threats.action: Enhance arboviral syndromic surveillance, improve differential diagnostic capacity at point-of-care, and intensify Aedes mosquito vector control

amrSignals: Bordetella pertussis resurgence with two alerts within three months may reflect circulating strains with altered antibiotic susceptibility profiles or vaccine-escape mutations warranting genomic surveillance
Sustained H5N1 circulation across avian and mammalian hosts increases opportunities for reassortment events that could produce antiviral-resistant variants
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory co-circulation (influenza, RSV, pertussis) creating compounded healthcare burden across both hemispheres
Arboviral threat convergence in the Americas with dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever alerts issued within weeks of each other suggesting shared vector pressure
Accelerating PAHO alert frequency in early 2026 compared to late 2025 indicates deteriorating epidemiological baseline across the Americas
H5N1 persistence across two consecutive PAHO reporting cycles (November 2025 and March 2026) signals endemic establishment in animal reservoirs rather than transient incursion
Immunization gap exploitation by measles and pertussis consistent with post-pandemic vaccination coverage deficits in multiple countries
